title: Initial ideals are stable under small perturbations of a presentation and its relations
statement: Let $(P,\mathfrak q)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means that $\mathfrak q$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $r,t\geq0$, let $b:P^r\to P$ be the row $(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$, and let $K:P^t\to P^r$ be a matrix, both acting by matrix multiplication on finite free modules. Suppose $\operatorname{im}K=\ker b$. Then there is an integer $h\geq1$ such that, for every row $b^{\prime}$ and matrix $K^{\prime}$ of these same sizes with all coefficients of $b-b^{\prime}$ and $K-K^{\prime}$ in $\mathfrak q^h$ and with $b^{\prime}K^{\prime}=0$, the ideals $J=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ and $J^{\prime}=(b^{\prime}_1,\ldots,b^{\prime}_r)$ satisfy, for every $d\geq0$, $$\mathfrak q^{d+1}+(J\cap\mathfrak q^d)=\mathfrak q^{d+1}+(J^{\prime}\cap\mathfrak q^d).$$ Here $\mathfrak q^0=P$ and subsequent powers are products of ideals.

source.place: Tags 07VE (lemma-approximate-complex) and 07VF (lemma-approximate-complex-graded), with L=P^t, M=P^r, N=P and I the maximal ideal; the equality is the displayed common-subquotient equality in the proof of 07VF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $\operatorname{im}K\subseteq P^r$ and $\operatorname{im}b\subseteq P$. Choose a common enlarged bound $c\geq0$. For either map $u:U\to V$ this gives $\operatorname{im}u\cap\mathfrak q^nV\subseteq\mathfrak q^{n-c}\operatorname{im}u=u(\mathfrak q^{n-c}U)$ for $n\geq c$: the last equality follows by lifting each summand $ay$ of the submodule product to $ax$ with $u(x)=y$. Set $h=c+1$, which depends only on $b,K$.

source.place: Tags 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees) and 00IO (lemma-map-AR), proof: apply Artin-Rees to the image and lift scalar multiples.

proof.text: Fix $b',K'$ as in the statement. Coefficient congruence implies $(K-K')(P^t)\subseteq\mathfrak q^{c+1}P^r$ and $(b-b')(P^r)\subseteq\mathfrak q^{c+1}$. The finite free modules are finitely generated, and $\mathfrak q$ is contained in every maximal ideal since it is the unique one. Apply [lem-sfb-perturbed-image-artin-rees-bound] with $(A,I,L,M,N,f,g,f',g')=(P,\mathfrak q,P^t,P^r,P,K,b,K',b')$ and the bounds of step 1. Exactness is $\operatorname{im}K=\ker b$; the perturbed complex condition is precisely $b'K'=0$. Thus $J'\cap\mathfrak q^n\subseteq b'(\mathfrak q^{n-c}P^r)$ for $n\geq c$.

source.place: Tag 07VE (lemma-approximate-complex), first conclusion and first paragraph of the proof: preservation of the Artin-Rees bound for the right differential; no use of the additional exactness conclusion.

proof.text: Fix $d\geq0$. If $d\leq c$, take $y=b(a)\in J\cap\mathfrak q^d$ and put $y'=b'(a)$. Then $y-y'\in\mathfrak q^{c+1}\subseteq\mathfrak q^{d+1}$, so $y'\in J'\cap\mathfrak q^d$. Conversely start with $y'=b'(a)\in J'\cap\mathfrak q^d$ and put $y=b(a)$; the same difference estimate gives $y\in J\cap\mathfrak q^d$. Adding $\mathfrak q^{d+1}$ yields the required equality in these degrees.

source.place: Tag 07VF (lemma-approximate-complex-graded), proof, the case n <= c.

proof.text: If $d>c$, step 1 writes any $y\in J\cap\mathfrak q^d$ as $b(a)$ with $a\in\mathfrak q^{d-c}P^r$. Put $y'=b'(a)$. Each coordinate of $a$ belongs to $\mathfrak q^{d-c}$, so the coefficient congruence gives $y-y'\in\mathfrak q^{c+1}\mathfrak q^{d-c}=\mathfrak q^{d+1}$. Hence $y'\in J'\cap\mathfrak q^d$. Conversely step 2 writes any $y'\in J'\cap\mathfrak q^d$ as $b'(a)$ with $a\in\mathfrak q^{d-c}P^r$; putting $y=b(a)$ gives the same estimate and $y\in J\cap\mathfrak q^d$. Thus each intersection lies in the other plus $\mathfrak q^{d+1}$, which proves equality of the two sums.

source.place: Tag 07VF (lemma-approximate-complex-graded), proof, n > c and the symmetric inclusion using the bound for g-prime.

lean.statement: theorem exists_adic_relation_matrix_initial_ideals {P : Type u} [CommRing P] [IsNoetherianRing P] [IsLocalRing P] (q : Ideal P) [q.IsMaximal] {r t : ℕ} (b : Fin r → P) (K : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin t) P) (h_exact : Function.Exact (Matrix.mulVec K) (dotProduct b)) : ∃ h : ℕ, 1 ≤ h ∧ ∀ (b' : Fin r → P) (K' : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin t) P), (∀ i : Fin r, b i - b' i ∈ q ^ h) → (∀ (i : Fin r) (j : Fin t), K i j - K' i j ∈ q ^ h) → Matrix.vecMul b' K' = 0 → ∀ d : ℕ, q ^ (d + 1) + (Ideal.span (Set.range b) ⊓ q ^ d) = q ^ (d + 1) + (Ideal.span (Set.range b') ⊓ q ^ d)
